question: what is the technology behind spoofing apps
answer: The technology behind spoofing apps primarily involves VoIP (Voice-over-Internet-Protocol) technology, which enables voice communications over the internet, allowing for easy manipulation of Caller ID information [p_d0692237237e214e45f6]. Additionally, spoofing can be achieved through methods like emulating the Bell 202 FSK signal (orange boxing) or accessing the SS7 network to make calls appear to originate from another number [p_cff38286a9d88db1a72f]. In app install fraud, SDK spoofing or replay attacks are used, where malicious actors mimic communication from a legitimate app installation [p_949db4d42be13281e4ad]. These technologies enable the disguise of identity in calls or digital interactions, though their misuse can be illegal [p_cff38286a9d88db1a72f].

VOIP offers a great deal more opportunity for call spoofing than standard PSTN. Using this technology in order to participate in pranks is now breaking the law. However, call spoofing services themselves remain legal. The technology is allowed, it is the way in which it is used which can be prosecuted. Less common, but also available are call spoofing technologies that emulate the Bell 202 FSK signal (also referred to as orange boxing), as well as switch access to the SS7 network so that it appears - even to telephone company operators - that a call is being placed by another existing phone number.
